content: It includes details about studies, authors, publication years, journals, and topics related to hepatitis C virus (HCV) treatment, often in combination with other conditions like HIV co-infection or cirrhosis. 1. Ledipasvir and Sofosbuvir have been studied for their efficacy in treating hepatitis C virus (HCV) in patients co-infected with HIV-1. The findings were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2015, volume 373, issue 8, pages 705-713. 2. Nehra VT, Rizza S, and Temesgen Z evaluated the fixed-dose combination of Ledipasvir and Sofosbuvir for the treatment of HCV genotype 4 infection. Their findings were published in Drugs of Today in 2016, volume 52, issue 2, pages 111-117. 3. Nelson D, Feld J, Kowdley KV, et al. conducted the Phase 3 FUSION trial, which assessed all-oral therapy with Sofosbuvir and Ribavirin for 12 or 16 weeks in treatment-experienced patients with HCV genotypes 2 and 3. The results were presented at the International Liver Congress in Amsterdam in 2013. 4. Nelson DR, Lalezari J, Pockros P, et al. investigated a 12-week all-oral regimen of Daclatasvir plus Sofosbuvir in patients with HCV genotype 3 infection. This study, known as the ALLY-3 Phase III study, was published in Hepatology in 2015, volume 61, issue 4, pages 1127-1135. 5. Nguyen MH, Trinh HN, Do ST, and Nguyen T conducted a multicenter open-label clinical trial to evaluate an 8-week regimen of Ledipasvir/Sofosbuvir (LDV/SOF) in treatment-naïve, non-cirrhotic patients with HCV genotype 6, and a 12-week regimen in those with cirrhosis or prior treatment failure. The findings were presented at the 26th Annual Conference of the Asian Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver (APASL) in 2017, published in Hepatology International, volume 11, supplement 1, page S105. 6. Nicoll A, Zeuzem S, Ghalib R, et al. reported the final SVR24 data from the Phase 3 C-EDGE treatment-naïve study, which evaluated the combination of Elbasvir (EBR) and Grazoprevir (GZR) in patients with chronic HCV genotypes 1, 4, or 6. The results were published in the Journal of Gastroenterology and Hepatology in 2016, volume 31, issue 80. 7. Ogawa E, Furusyo N, Nomura H, et al. demonstrated that NS5A resistance-associated variants reduce the effectiveness of Ledipasvir and Sofosbuvir in cirrhotic patients with HCV genotype 1b. This study was published in the Journal of Gastroenterology in 2017, volume 52, issue 7, pages 845-854. 8. Ogawa E, Furusyo N, Nomura H, et al. also evaluated the safety and efficacy of Sofosbuvir plus Ledipasvir in HCV genotype 1b patients with compensated cirrhosis. The findings were presented at the 26th APASL Annual Conference in 2017, published in Hepatology International, volume 11, supplement 1, page S1012. 9. Ogawa E, Furusyo N, Yamashita N, et al. assessed the safety and efficacy of Daclatasvir plus Asunaprevir in patients aged 75 years and older with HCV genotype 1b, with or without cirrhosis. The study was published in Hepatology Research in 2017, volume 47, issue 3, pages E120-E131. 10. O'Leary J, Brown RS, Reddy KR, et al. identified baseline clinical and laboratory parameters associated with the clinical benefits of successful HCV treatment using Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir in decompensated cirrhotic patients. The findings were presented at the 51st Annual Meeting of the European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL) in 2016, published in the Journal of Hepatology, volume 64, supplement 2, page S774. 11. Osinusi A, Townsend K, Kohli A, et al. reported on the virologic response following combined administration of Ledipasvir and Sofosbuvir in patients with HCV genotype 1 and HIV co-infection. The study was published in JAMA in 2015, volume 313, issue 12, pages 1232-1239. 12. Patrick Basu P, Shah NJ, John N, et al. conducted a single-center prospective open-label clinical pilot study to evaluate the efficacy of Sofosbuvir and Ledipasvir in achieving SVR12 in a subpopulation of sickle cell disease patients with chronic HCV. The study was presented at a surgical endoscopy conference in 2017. 13. Pearlman B, Lutchman G, Shiffman ML, et al. assessed the safety and efficacy of Elbasvir and Grazoprevir, with or without Ribavirin, for treating HCV genotype 1. The results were published in the Journal of Hepatology in 2017, volume 66, page S294. 14. Persico M, Aglitti A, Caruso R, et al. evaluated the efficacy and safety of new direct-acting antiviral agents in HCV-infected patients with diffuse large B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The findings were published in Hepatology in 2017, volume 17, page 17. 15. Pianko S, Flamm SL, Shiffman ML, et al. investigated the combination therapy of Sofosbuvir plus Velpatasvir in treatment-experienced patients with HCV genotypes 1 or 3. The study was published in the Annals of Internal Medicine in 2015, volume 163, issue 11, pages 809-817.
